{"local_delta": 0.00,
 "departures": [
  {"fact": "England's services, searches and custody allocation operate on the biological-sex definitions fixed by the UK Supreme Court's 16 April 2025 judgment on 'woman'/'sex' in the Equality Act 2010.",
   "local_evidence": "The local bundle itself states: \"The definitions that govern services, searches and detention allocation in England were fixed by the national supreme court's unanimous judgment handed down 16 April 2025\"; item: \"the unanimous judgment of the country's highest court (handed down 16 April 2025) that 'woman' and 'sex' in the Equality Act 2010 refer to biological woman and biological sex\".",
   "direction": "riskier",
   "magnitude": 0.0,
   "visitor_applicability": "Reaches visitors (service refusal, facility access, strip-search/custody basis), but it is the national regime, not an England-only departure.",
   "already_in_national_bundle": true,
   "counted_in_delta": false},
  {"fact": "EHRC code of practice of 20 May 2025 lets providers request a birth certificate on \"genuine concern\" about biological sex and exclude trans people from single-sex sport \"when necessary\"; described locally as the operative guidance a visitor meets at venues, transport and services.",
   "local_evidence": "\"the national equality and human-rights commission ... updated its code of practice on 20 May 2025 ... services and businesses may ask a person for a birth certificate where there is 'genuine concern' about biological sex, and that trans people may be excluded from single-sex sport 'when necessary' for safety.\"",
   "direction": "riskier",
   "magnitude": 0.0,
   "visitor_applicability": "Yes — venue/service-level, applies to a trans visitor; but the authoring body is national (England and Wales) and the guidance duplicates the national single-sex-spaces guidance.",
   "already_in_national_bundle": true,
   "counted_in_delta": false},
  {"fact": "Prison/custody accommodation by biological sex, upheld in the ruling striking down identity-based prison guidance; a judicial review heard 5 February 2026 argues a blanket birth-sex rule breaches human rights and creates suicide risk.",
   "local_evidence": "\"a judge ruled that guidance of a prison service allowing some trans prisoners to be housed by gender identity is unlawful\"; \"no outcome of that hearing is documented in the sources used here\".",
   "direction": "riskier",
   "magnitude": 0.0,
   "visitor_applicability": "Only if a visitor is detained; the same litigation is already recorded at national level and its outcome is unresolved.",
   "already_in_national_bundle": true,
   "counted_in_delta": false},
  {"fact": "Official hate-crime baseline for England and a neighbouring component: 115,990 police-recorded hate crimes in the year to March 2025, transgender strand down 11% year on year.",
   "local_evidence": "\"Official statistics for this state/province and a neighbouring component (published 9 October 2025): 115,990 police-recorded hate crimes ... transgender strand down 11% ... no population denominator ... earlier years over-counted.\"",
   "direction": "safer",
   "magnitude": 0.0,
   "visitor_applicability": "No — raw count without denominator, covers residents' reporting behaviour, and the bundle expressly says it supports no per-capita comparison; cannot outweigh tier-1 national exposures.",
   "already_in_national_bundle": false,
   "counted_in_delta": false}
 ],
 "inherited_national_exposure": [
  "National Equality Act biological-sex interpretation (Supreme Court, 16 April 2025) and the EHRC code of practice built on it — inherited, governs England directly.",
  "National strip-search policy for transport police (trans women searched by officers of sex at birth, interim position, April 2025) — inherited.",
  "National prison-placement litigation (For Women Scotland-type ruling; 5 February 2026 judicial review argument on suicide risk) — inherited, unresolved.",
  "National health-service ward policy (trans patients to be excluded from sex-based wards), the Joëlle case and the national clinical review's minor-prescribing restrictions — inherited national climate.",
  "National gendered-spaces harassment survey and rising anti-trans media rhetoric; rainbow-index fall from 1st/86% (2015) to 22nd/45% (2025) — inherited climate signal.",
  "Gender Recognition Act machinery, GRC recognition withdrawal for 50 foreign jurisdictions, and NHS/healthcare infrastructure — resident-facing, inherited, not re-counted."
 ],
 "uncertainty": "The local bundle adds no England-only fact: every item is either explicitly national (Supreme Court ruling, EHRC code, interior-department bulletin) or duplicated from the national dossier. The 5 February 2026 prison judicial review outcome is unresolved, a regional police searching policy remains unretrieved (HTTP 403), and no England-specific trans hate-crime count or rate exists — so no evidentiary basis for a signed local departure in either direction.",
 "notes": "A delta of 0.00 here is a diagnostic of evidentiary duplication, not proof that England is equal to the national level or that the regime is benign. The operative driver — the biological-sex definitions governing services, searches and custody, plus the equality-body code permitting birth-certificate requests on 'genuine concern' — is expressly attributed in the local bundle to the national framework and therefore already priced into 0.443529. The only items not literally in the national dossier (the England-and-Wales hate-crime bulletin) are raw counts without a denominator, explicitly non-comparable, and a declining transgender strand that cannot offset tier-1 universal-exposure measures; they are recorded but not counted."}
